# Trellis For Rust Consumers

Use with [the consumer guide](llms-full.txt) from the same Trellis revision.
Trellis does not prescribe an application's configuration parser, database,
domain types, DI pattern, logging setup, or test framework.

## Generated Package

Administrative Auth callers consume the generated `trellis.auth@v1` actions.
`Users.Update` has optional `username` for an atomic local-login rename that
preserves the principal ID and password; collisions roll back profile changes.
`Users.PasswordReset.Create` targets `userId` and returns a time-limited, one-use
account-flow link. `UserIdentities.List`, `UserIdentities.Unlink`, and
`Users.IdentityLink.Create` accept optional `userId`; omission targets the caller,
and another user's identities require platform administration. Last-method and
protected-account safeguards remain. `Connections.List` accepts `principalId`.
Declare these actions in native IDL and use generated request models/facades;
capability-group presets saved through `Grants.Set` are exact snapshots, not live
group memberships.
Exact snapshots can initiate resource provisioning without bypassing runtime
readiness. Resource actions stay within the snapshot and delegation ceiling;
read-only approval does not grant write access.

Author native IDL and set `[package]`, `[sources]`, and `[generate.rust].output`
in `trellis.toml`. `trellis generate` is offline after dependencies are
available in the global validated source-package cache.
A durable `consumer` requires a direct `trellis` source package dependency
containing `trellis.events@v1`; select and lock its version before generation.

The output is one ordinary crate at the source package version, with
`orders_trellis::apis::<api>` and `orders_trellis::participants::<participant>`
modules, not independent SDK or participant crates. Add an ordinary Cargo path
dependency, for example `orders-trellis = { path = "trellis" }`. The generated
crate declares the published runtime dependency matching the CLI. It has no
generator build script, repository-relative runtime paths, or runtime-path
config in `trellis.toml`. Use ordinary Cargo overrides when developing against a
local runtime. Generation does not modify the consumer's Cargo manifest.

Commit generated output when clones should build with Cargo alone, without the
Trellis CLI/cache. Regenerate rather than editing it. Native source packages,
not canonical API/participant JSON, are the publication and evidence boundary.

An API SDK contains types and descriptors. The participant facade supplies the
connection boundary and only the declared caller/provider surfaces. Its
constants carry source-package/participant evidence; applications do not supply
digests to service bootstrap.

## Connection

Service facades export `connect` and `ServiceConnectOptions`. The current
constructor takes only Trellis URL and the provisioned identity seed; name and
timeout are optional builders:

```rust
let mut service = connect(
    ServiceConnectOptions::new(&trellis_url, &identity_seed)
        .with_name("orders-service")
        .with_timeout_ms(10_000),
).await?;
```

Trellis resolves deployment/instance assignment, installed package/participant
evidence, exact grants, resources, signed context, route JWT, and endpoints
server-side. Authorization state is process-memory-only and is refreshed
proactively as SDK-owned maintenance. Renewing unchanged transport authority
promotes context and routing credentials without replacing a healthy socket.
Newly approved authority is adopted automatically on a readied successor; safe
accepted work retains its receiving connection until it settles. No manual
transport-refresh API, upgrade notification, or context-store parameter exists.
Retain generated facades, still-bound resources, and job references across
handoffs. While own revocation coverage is unavailable, fresh application IO
either waits within its acquisition budget or reports unavailability.
Guarded registry maintenance restores
coverage and wakes calls without requiring a new socket. Watch migration keeps
cached authority and existing leases, while actual revocation, reduced authority,
and hard deadlines remain fail-closed. Raw NATS access is physical, not a logical
generation-aware facade.

Register generated providers before `service.run().await`. The service lifecycle
supervises its request host and workers. `with_timeout_ms(...)` bounds
bootstrap, connect, and request operations.

Apps/agents use user-login credentials (login session ID plus session seed) and
perform context refresh before CONNECT. Devices retain their provisioned
identity seed and use generated activation/connect options. Do not substitute a
raw NATS URL/JWT or client-authored assignment for either lifecycle.

A generated device companion is established only through the parent device's
activation flow and separate user consent. It receives an independent ordinary
App/Agent user session and cannot bootstrap standalone or use the parent's
device authority.

## Typed Surfaces

Use the participant's generated methods. Dependency aliases are accessors on
`client()`; owned provider registration is under `handle()`. For the tutorial's
`orders` alias selecting RPC `Orders.Create`, use the generated
`connected.client().orders().orders_create(...)` method. Its argument type comes
from the generated API crate; it need not share the authored model's name.

Exact method and model names come from the generated crate. Match generated
declared-error variants directly; transport and unknown remote failures remain
distinct. Operations expose generated invokers and typed references for start,
wait, progress/watch, and optional cancellation/transfer.
Native no-responder replies become `ServiceUnavailableError`, exposed through
`CallError::ServiceUnavailable` or `TrellisClientError::ServiceUnavailable`.
They indicate that the requested service is not currently reachable, including
during a restart; they are not malformed protocol offers or declared domain errors.
Persist a caller-selected ULID before `start_with_invocation_id(id, &input)`;
this is the durable operation ID, recoverable through `control(id)`.
To cancel a reserved invocation that may not yet be admitted, use
`start_cancelled_with_invocation_id(id, &input)` with its original input. It
requires both Invoke and Cancel authority and atomically retains cancellation
intent before new handler entry. The returned reference does not imply finished
cleanup; explicitly `wait()` for the terminal result. Normal replay never clears
that intent; an existing terminal result is returned unchanged.

Owned event publication uses generated publishers. Durable handlers use declared
Consumer resources; Trellis resolves durable identity, local concurrency, retry,
authority, and scoped Events DLQ/replay. Delivery may repeat, so choose a
side-effect strategy that handles duplicates. Subjects include the encoded
qualified API identity and base64url parameter tokens; the signed descriptor
binds the exact API, dotted event name, and parameter count. Success is
acknowledged only after the handler succeeds;
final exhaustion is durably recorded before source acknowledgement. Manual
replay uses the same handler and a fresh retry budget without rewinding the
original Consumer, and confirms resolution before acknowledgement.

Jobs are private service queues. Use generated queue handles and cloneable
`jobs_client()` handles for submission from other handlers. Worker registration
and processing are supervised by the service lifecycle. Jobs expose durable
state, retries, progress, cooperative cancellation, and live updates. Delivery
progress acknowledgement is automatic. Waiting for keyed capacity extends the
current delivery and does not consume an attempt before handler entry.
`Jobs.Summary` computes all matching totals, groups, and statistics
independently of a `Jobs.Query` page.
Job deadlines are creation-relative. Omitted retry means five ordinary attempts with
delays of 5s, 30s, 2m, and 10m; explicit retry requires exactly one fewer
positive ordered backoffs than total attempts.
Broker redelivery is unlimited. Before business work, inspect
`job.cancellation_token().reason()`: already-cancelled job handlers must reconcile
earlier side effects. Cleanup errors preserve redelivery; previously started work reaches
Expired or Dead only after successful cleanup. Never-started expiration releases
any recovered key slot without running the handler. Ordinary queues use Block,
not an authored stale policy. Coordinator fail-stale takeover preserves cleanup
for a recovered owner with a fresh fence and `JobCancellationReason::StaleAttempt`;
only that owner settles Stale, without mutating the replacement owner's slot.

Operation get, watch, signal, and cancel remain bound to the creator principal
plus participant across reconnects rather than to one session key. A durable
Operation's watcher is a separate live session: it reconciles the current
authoritative snapshot once its transport is ready, then yields ordered typed
transient updates and terminal state; not-yet-delivered nonterminal snapshots may
be conflated, but transient updates are not silently dropped. Opening or closing
a watcher never starts, cancels, or completes the durable work. Completed,
failed, and cancelled records are immutable.
Rust operation handlers can clone `control.cancellation()` and observe
`Requested`, `OwnershipLost`, or `ServiceStopping` with `is_cancelled()`,
`reason()`, or `cancelled().await`. They must stop and join owned child work,
including already-running `spawn_blocking` closures, before returning from
requested cancellation. A healthy owner renews its lease and leaves cancellation
nonterminal while cleanup runs; the caller's `cancel()` resolves terminal
`Cancelled` only after cleanup and the fenced write. A cleanup handler error
leaves cancellation nonterminal for recovery. Recovered handlers enter with
`Requested` already set and must retry cleanup without starting new business
work; return `Ok(())` only after cleanup succeeds. External effects may still
overlap across owner loss; use idempotency or external fencing.

Live observations and Operation watchers are authorized live sessions negotiated with
bounded opening requests. The provider signs its offer and frames; control
responses bind the session ID, logical command sequence, and command hash, and
continued authority is rechecked from retained context rather than per-frame
network lookup. A session has protocol liveness and credit bounds, not a total
age or message cap. Closing returns a receipt whose remote-cleanup state is
complete, incomplete, or unconfirmed, and reconnect is an explicit new open
rather than a silent reopen.

## Resources And Atomicity

Use generated State, KV, Store, Consumer, and Job handles. State is one typed
value without key/TTL; KV is typed history; Store is raw bytes. State/KV direct
historical migration runs in SDK memory without write-on-read. Resolved binding
payloads and subjects are runtime internals.

Generated cursor-paginated RPCs add lazy fallible page/item streams. Missing
`next_cursor` is the sole end signal; general keyset pagination does not promise
a snapshot.

`StoreResourceHandle::list_page` and file metadata listing are key-sorted keyset
pagination with opaque cursors bound to the prefix query. The limit defaults to
100 and must be at most 500. Desired resource capacities are sizing hints,
approved commitments define authority, and generated bindings expose observed
provider limits. Trellis does not adopt or destroy foreign-owned physical
resources.

Store readers/writers support bounded streaming through `write_from` and
`read_into`; whole-buffer helpers remain available. Generated Operation
references upload bytes with `upload(body)`; lower-level operation builders
stream with `transfer_from(reader)` without a caller-supplied size or hash.
Trellis counts and hashes bytes while sending and verifies size and SHA-256 on
receipt; cancellation is authenticated and acknowledged.

Prepared events and SQL outbox stores allow event intents to participate in a
local SQL transaction. The application owns its transaction and migration
execution. KV outbox/inbox stores do not atomically commit unrelated database
writes. See `/guides/libraries/rust` and current Rustdoc for supported stores
and transaction APIs.

SQL outbox claims expire after 30 seconds and can be reclaimed. Pass the claimed
record to `mark_published`/`mark_failed`; false means ownership was superseded.
`dispatch_outbox_once` returns `ClaimLost` for superseded completion.
Publication can repeat after interruption, so the claim fence is not
exactly-once delivery. Current schema helpers do not upgrade pre-release
layouts; applications own migration of any retained older database.

## Test And Verify

Run generation and the consuming project's own Cargo checks. A real-runtime test
can launch a Rust service from a Deno test using `@oatscenter/trellis-testkit` and
its `TrellisTestRuntime`. A Rust test uses the published `trellis-testkit` crate,
which starts the released `trellis` and `trellis-server` executables out of
process, chooses its loopback ports automatically, and returns the existing SDK
connection options so your generated service and app facades connect normally.
Private Trellis workspace crates are never consumer dependencies; a service
repository depends on `trellis-rs` and `trellis-testkit` only.

Use `/api` to discover current Rustdoc and generated participant source for
project-specific APIs. Private Trellis workspace crates are not consumer
dependencies. Trellis's supported Rust toolchain is current stable.
